change: PowerPoint and CSV keep their text rank at the merge
why: PowerPoint gained; Excel and Word fell.

change: A 4B text reranker in place of the 149M one
why: Lower score, and about 14 times slower.

change: Tie-break on rare words from the question
why: The public score fell.

change: File name and page number added to what the reranker reads
why: The public score fell.

change: PDF pages merged again with their image rank after the rerank
why: Hard table pages fell.

change: Boost for PDF pages that hold the exact numbers in the question
why: PDFs fell.

change: PDF tables kept whole when the text is cut into chunks
why: Within noise.

change: Vision reranker on the top 10 PDF and slide pages
why: Slides gained; PDF table pages fell.

change: Vision reranker on the top 10 slides only
why: Slides gained, and no other file type moved.

change: At most 2 chunks in a row per file before the rerank
why: PowerPoint gained; overall flat.

change: Vision reranker looks at 30 slides, not 10
why: Large public gain, but 4 hard questions dropped a place or two. Kept as an option for slide folders on a GPU (decision 2026-10-14).

change: Image search counts double for slides at the merge
why: Slides gained; Excel, Word and PowerPoint fell.

change: Files named for a different quarter go behind the rest
why: No gain, even for slides.

change: Every Office page gets a picture, not only the first 4
why: PowerPoint gained; Excel fell.

change: Every Office page, and Office files reorder only among themselves
why: PowerPoint gained, but Word moved on 16 questions: 6 up, 10 down.

change: Every PowerPoint page, and PowerPoint files reorder only among themselves
why: Word is untouched, but the PowerPoint gain is within noise.

change: OCR for PDF regions with no text layer, tried on the normal PDFs
why: Normal PDFs barely move on the public set; hard PDF questions dip a little. Turn it on for a folder that may hold scans.

change: A stress test, not a change: every PDF turned into a scan, then read back with OCR
why: Without OCR a scanned PDF is never first. With OCR it is 1 point under a typed PDF on the public set; hard look-alike table questions lose more.

change: Page pictures vote only for pages with little text of their own
why: Word, Excel and PDF fell, and scanned pages were no longer found by their picture.

change: Swap the text embedder for mxbai-embed-large-v1 (a production option), text-only with the reranker
why: A tie with the current embedder when the reranker is on. The top 10 is 2 to 3 points lower for Word, PDF, PowerPoint and Excel.

change: Spreadsheet chunks that carry the sheet name, a summary of the columns and the header row
why: Excel moves within noise, Word falls a little, and the hard set falls.

change: A big workbook shares its 300 chunk slots across all its sheets, so no sheet is left out of the index
why: Excel gains and the hard set does not move. The gain comes from one workbook whose later sheets were never indexed. Adopted on 2026-10-13.

change: Swap the text embedder for EmbeddingGemma 2 (new from Google, Apache-2.0), text-only with the reranker
why: A tie with the current embedder for Word, PDF, PowerPoint and Excel. It finds more slide images by their text, and it scores above mxbai.

change: Use EmbeddingGemma 2 as the page-picture model in place of the current one: one vector for a whole page, not one for each patch of it
why: Lower on both question sets. Word and PDF lose most. One vector does not hold the detail of a full page.

change: The same as M30, with 4 times the picture detail (1,120 image tokens per page, the most the model allows)
why: Still lower on both question sets. More detail did not help: with pictures alone it scored a little lower than at the default detail.

change: A 4 times bigger vision reranker (8B) reorders the top 10 PDF pages and slides by their pictures
why: No gain on the public set, and look-alike PDF table pages still fall on the hard set, as with the smaller model. Not worth a GPU for this.

change: Look up table rows that match the question (row label, column header, values) and move the best page of a file to the front
why: PDF questions fall on the public set: rows matched only by country and year labels repeat on every annex page. Pages that hold a value from the question gained.

change: With agent mode on, an LLM (Claude Haiku) reads the text of the top 10 pages and puts the page that holds the answer first
why: Passes the table rule: table-cell questions +0.166 (CI above 0), public set does not fall, hard set +0.042. Needs an LLM, so it is the +agent step and stays off by default.

change: With agent mode on, when the LLM finds no page, it writes two new search queries, search runs for each, the lists are merged, and the LLM reads the new top 10 pages once more
why: No gain: 1 question better, 5 worse on the public set, hard set unchanged. The new queries bring new pages but rarely the right one. Costs about 2 more LLM calls on 1 in 8 questions.

change: With agent mode on, the LLM step also opens when the top 5 pages hold 2 slides of one deck, and then the LLM reads the top 20 pages instead of 10
why: Worse on the public set: 6 questions better, 25 worse, all slides. The LLM often names a wrong slide over the right one that plain search had first. Hard set unchanged within its interval.

change: An LLM (Claude Haiku) writes one context line per chunk at index time, for keyword search, the embedding and the reranker; trial on 183 files
why: No gain on held-out questions (+0.018, interval includes 0); hard set -0.018. The public gain is from slides that got a line while their look-alikes did not.

change: An LLM (Claude Haiku) writes one context line for every slide image at index time (enrich mode), for keyword search, the embedding and the reranker
why: Slides better: right slide first 155 -> 170 of 223. Other file types unchanged. Hard set: one slide question lost, one gained. Needs an LLM at index time; all test slides are one company's decks.
